messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genotype frequencies by individual
parts:
Pull out the genotypes as a matrix, and then calculate the proportion of 1's (or 2's) in each row. You could plot a histogram.

g <- pull.geno(mycross)
propAA <- rowMeans(g==1, na.rm=TRUE)
hist(propAA, breaks=50)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genotype frequencies by individual
parts:
Thank you Sir for the help extended.

I have installed qtlbim.

I was trying to read in the Bayesian Interval Mapping results from Cartographer following this link: http://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~yandell/qtl/software/qtlbim/

which read as following


Bmapqtl module of QTLCartographer. The output of the Bmapqtl can be the input to R/bim via the read.bim() routine. Currently that is a bit of a kludge, requiring a file called nval.dat. You may have to do the following: 
> library(bim)
## Initialize options.
> bmapqtl.options()
## Write options to file "nval.dat". You can modify values using
## write.bmapqtl() or later edit the file by hand.
> write.bmapqtl()
## Read your Bmapqtl file created from QTLCart.
> mybim <- read.bim(".", "yourbmapqtlfilename")
## Summary and plot.
> summary(mybim)
> plot(mybim)



Should i replace the package "bim" with "qtlbim" instead ? My data is from Doubled haploid individuals made from two mustard plants.

Please understand that i am new to R and i do not intend to bother you unless i have tried all the ways by myself including a search on this R-group.

Thank you in anticipation Sir.

Thank you very much.
